boards.title: Your First Weekend at Grinnell College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence combining first-year arrival tasks, campus resources, public art, and nearby outdoor stops. Confirm live schedules before setting out.

cards.title: Friday: Pick Up Your Key and P-Card
cards.subtitle: Start the weekend at official new-student check-in
cards.notes: Bring the documents listed in your arrival instructions, collect your key and P-Card, then follow the assigned unloading route.
cards.short_summary: Make Harris Center the practical first stop before moving into your residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College says first-year check-in begins at the Harris Center, where students receive their room key, P-Card, and orientation materials.
cards.access_notes: The current 2026 arrival page lists check-in beginning at 8 a.m. Friday, Aug. 21, 2026; use the arrival map for parking and unloading.

cards.title: Friday: Learn the Dining-Hall Rhythm
cards.subtitle: Use your first meal to locate the JRC dining stations
cards.notes: Check NutriSlice for the current menu, bring your P-Card, and note the shorter Friday dinner window before making evening plans.
cards.short_summary: A first Marketplace meal introduces the main campus dining location and its weekend schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Marketplace Dining Hall is in the Joe Rosenfield ’25 Center and serves students, campus members, and guests; the academic-year Friday schedule runs until 7:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: During the academic year, Friday hours are 7 a.m.–7:30 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday use separate meal periods. Check detailed hours for exceptions.

cards.title: Friday Night: Find the Campus Late-Night Counter
cards.subtitle: Locate an evening food option inside the JRC
cards.notes: Walk through the JRC before it gets late, identify the service counter and seating, and confirm the day’s closing time online.
cards.short_summary: Spencer Grill provides a clearly documented evening option during the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell Dining identifies Spencer Grill as a JRC venue serving beverages, bakery items, snacks, and made-to-order food, with academic-year weekend service.
cards.access_notes: Current academic-year hours list Friday and Saturday closing at 10:30 p.m. and Sunday service from 9 a.m.–10:30 p.m.; verify exceptions before going.

cards.title: Saturday Morning: Map Your Study Options
cards.subtitle: Tour the main library before coursework accelerates
cards.notes: Locate the circulation desk, compare collaborative and quiet zones, and save the library contact and live-hours page on your phone.
cards.short_summary: An early library walkthrough makes future research and study choices easier.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College Libraries identifies Burling as a main campus library with research help, collections, technology, and quiet and collaborative study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary and are displayed through the library’s live-hours system. Campus users should check the library homepage before visiting.

cards.title: Saturday: Learn Campus Through Public Art
cards.subtitle: Follow the college’s named outdoor sculpture route
cards.notes: Open the official tour on your phone, choose several works along your normal campus paths, and photograph labels for later reference.
cards.short_summary: The sculpture route turns an ordinary campus walk into a visual orientation exercise.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College publishes a Campus Sculpture Tour featuring outdoor works encountered across campus and beyond.
cards.access_notes: The tour is outdoors; follow posted campus access rules and account for weather, construction, and daylight.

cards.title: Saturday Afternoon: Step Into GCMoA
cards.subtitle: Add a free indoor arts stop at Bucksbaum
cards.notes: Enter through Bucksbaum, check the current exhibition listing, and leave enough time to view labels instead of rushing the galleries.
cards.short_summary: GCMoA supplies a structured indoor stop after the outdoor sculpture route.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell College Museum of Art states that it is free and open to all, with Saturday gallery hours during its posted semester schedule.
cards.source_title: Visit the Museum of Art | Grinnell College
cards.access_notes: The current visit page lists Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 1–5 p.m., and closure Sunday and Monday. Check for semester changes.

cards.title: Saturday: Walk Downtown to Central Park
cards.subtitle: Use the gazebo and playground as downtown landmarks
cards.notes: Walk the route in daylight, identify the gazebo and accessible restroom area, and note where campus gives way to downtown blocks.
cards.short_summary: Central Park provides an easy landmark for learning the downtown layout.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Grinnell identifies Central Park Gazebo at 925 3rd Avenue within a 3.8-acre community park with a playground and accessible restrooms.
cards.access_notes: The city states that all parks are closed daily from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. Public use may be affected by scheduled events or reservations.

cards.title: Sunday Afternoon: Get a Town Library Landmark
cards.subtitle: Visit the public library just south of campus
cards.notes: Browse the public areas, review upcoming programs, and record the weekend schedule so you have a non-campus study option.
cards.short_summary: Drake Community Library connects the weekend route with a practical town resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College’s current visitor guide lists Drake Community Library at 930 Park Street and provides year-round Saturday and Sunday hours.
cards.source_title: Arts and Culture | Grinnell College Visitor Guide
cards.access_notes: The visitor guide lists Saturday hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday hours of 2–5 p.m.; verify holiday or special closures directly.

cards.title: Sunday: Take a Longer Recreation Loop
cards.subtitle: Explore a named park north of central Grinnell
cards.notes: Choose the walking path or an open court, bring water, and obey construction signs rather than entering any restricted park area.
cards.short_summary: Ahrens Park expands the weekend beyond campus with multiple outdoor recreation choices.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell’s visitor guide describes Ahrens Park as having courts, fields, playgrounds, green space, shelters, and a 1.5-mile outdoor walking path.
cards.source_title: Recreation and Entertainment | Grinnell College Visitor Guide
cards.access_notes: The guide warns that construction may place some areas off-limits. Follow signs and confirm current facility conditions before using courts or fields.

cards.title: Future Weekend: Save CERA for a Planned Outing
cards.subtitle: Close the card sequence with an off-campus nature option
cards.notes: Download the official trail map, arrange transportation with classmates, check weather, and stay on designated public routes.
cards.short_summary: CERA becomes a follow-up weekend plan once transportation and trail conditions are settled.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College describes CERA as a 365-acre field station open to the public for hiking, birdwatching, photography, art, and quiet enjoyment.
cards.source_title: Recreation and Entertainment | Grinnell College Visitor Guide
cards.access_notes: CERA is approximately 11 miles from campus. The College states that local taxis, ride-share services, and public transportation are unavailable, so plan a safe ride.

warnings: Museum hours differ across some older university pages; the dedicated current visit page was used.
Live library hours and temporary closures should be checked immediately before visiting.
CERA requires advance transportation planning because it is off campus.
